upstream_gpu_facts.xpu_definition: Vector (CPU SIMD) mode with occlusion-ray processing offloaded to GPU; not a standalone full GPU path tracer. Per OpenMoonRay's own Sept 2024 SIGGRAPH BoF post, full direct/indirect-ray GPU processing was still in development at that time; no later official status update was found.
upstream_gpu_facts.nvidia_gpu_code_path: moonray repo, lib/rendering/rt/gpu/optix/ (OptixGPUAccelerator.cc/h, OptixGPUPrograms.cu, etc.). No separate plain-CUDA-without-OptiX path exists.

build_flags.MOONRAY_USE_OPTIX: current authoritative flag gating both CUDA toolkit and OptiX requirement
build_flags.MOONRAY_USE_CUDA: superseded/historical flag name seen in older community posts, not present in current main CMakeLists
build_flags.MOONRAY_USE_METAL: Apple Silicon GPU path, unrelated to NVIDIA

upstream_gpu_facts.optix_version_pinned: 7.6 exactly (official docs state MoonRay is not yet compatible with newer OptiX releases)
upstream_gpu_facts.min_gpu_architecture: UNKNOWN -- no official source found; no compute-capability check exists in code
upstream_gpu_facts.cpu_xpu_feature_parity: Not full parity. XPU matches vector mode pixel-for-pixel where supported, but inherits vector mode's own gaps vs scalar mode (no physically-correct overlapping dielectrics, no variance buffers, no volume+deep combination) plus XPU-specific gaps (round bezier curves, round curves/meshes with >2 motion samples). Documented automatic silent fallback to CPU vector mode on insufficient GPU memory or GPU init failure.
upstream_gpu_facts.wsl2_status: CPU/vector-mode builds are reported working on WSL2 by the community in OpenMoonRay's own official Discussions (#90, #183, #211). OptiX/XPU is reported explicitly non-functional on WSL2 in the same official Discussions (#90, Apr 2023, citing NVIDIA forum threads), with no later official-repo evidence of a fix through Sept 2025 (#211). No official DreamWorks/OpenMoonRay statement declares WSL2 officially supported for either mode.
upstream_gpu_facts.rtx_3060_assessment: Architecture/compute capability (Ampere, CC 8.6) is well above the documented Pascal-and-later floor for CUDA-on-WSL2 and would very likely satisfy MoonRay's requirements on native Linux; no official minimum architecture blocks it. On WSL2 specifically, OptiX/XPU should be treated as not currently workable per available evidence -- the blocker is the WSL2 OptiX runtime, not the RTX 3060's own capability.
upstream_gpu_facts.blender_hydra_moonray_status: Per OpenMoonRay's own official Discussion #211 (Sept 2025), referencing the cjhosken/mfb project directly: RDLA export works, hd_render (standalone) works, but 'rendering with hydra doesn't work' inside Blender. No official or community evidence found of MoonRay ever rendering successfully inside Blender via any path (Hydra or direct).
